summary: The President [reaffirmed a fully digitalised electronic-government target for 2030](2026-08-04-president-herminie-receives-credentials-from-maltas-first-high-commissioner-to-seychelles) while receiving a foreign envoy's credentials, exploring bilateral technical cooperation.
developments:
The restatement came in August 2026 at a credentials ceremony ([target](2026-08-04-president-herminie-receives-credentials-from-maltas-first-high-commissioner-to-seychelles)).

No strategy document, delivery plan, milestone set or budget for the target is held at any date. What the base can show against it is a relaunched portal, an electronic case management system, a certificate of origin, a business one-stop portal in pilot, and an invoicing system at procurement — five services, no plan.

summary: A [national science, technology and innovation institute](2025-12-23-gazette-nisti-act) was established by Act with an artificial-intelligence strategy mandate, and the body was [reinstated under the Vice-President](2026-08-10-seychelles-nisti-reinstatement-digitalisation-priority) while no commencement notice for the Act is on record.
developments:
The Act was assented in December 2025, establishing a body corporate with an artificial-intelligence strategy mandate, a science academy, an open-access scientific-data repository and incubation centres ([Act](2025-12-23-gazette-nisti-act)).

The institute was reinstated with its secretariat under the Office of the Vice-President and is described as functioning; no commencement notice for the Act is cited anywhere ([reinstatement](2026-08-10-seychelles-nisti-reinstatement-digitalisation-priority)).

A body operating under a statute whose commencement cannot be evidenced is worth stating plainly. No artificial-intelligence strategy has been produced under the mandate; what exists instead is an education framework, recorded separately.

summary: The [Data Protection Act 2023](2023-12-22-seychelles-data-protection-act-2023-act-24) is in force in full, its eighteen-month transition having elapsed, and it expressly recognises participation in a global cross-border privacy system.
developments:
The Act commenced in December 2023 with an eighteen-month transition; that period has elapsed and controllers and processors are now subject to it in full ([Act](2023-12-22-seychelles-data-protection-act-2023-act-24), [force](2024-03-25 Data Protection Law Now In Force In Seychelles), [review](2024-06-04 Review of Seychelles DPA)).

A continental review adds that the Act expressly recognises participation in a global cross-border privacy rules system ([reforms](2026-03-12 Africa’s Data Protection Reforms A Continental Perspective on the Drivers of Change in Legal Frameworks)).

A statute fully in force with an explicit cross-border interoperability provision puts this unit ahead of most in the frame on the law. What it lacks is recorded in the next cell.

summary: An [access-to-information reform whitepaper](2025-11-10-infocom-atia-reform-whitepaper) recommends a centralised access unit, alignment with the data-protection Act and open-reuse licensing, with drafting targeted for end-2025.
developments:
The whitepaper was published in November 2025 with drafting by the attorney-general targeted for the end of that year ([whitepaper](2025-11-10-infocom-atia-reform-whitepaper)).

Nothing has entered the base since, so the drafting target has passed with no draft on record. The same body holds both the access and the protection mandates, which is why the whitepaper proposes aligning the two statutes rather than treating them separately.

summary: The Information Commission names [no clear power to enforce its orders](2025-11-10-infocom-atia-reform-whitepaper) as its own most urgent weakness, in its own reform whitepaper.
developments:
The finding is the Commission's own, set out in its access-to-information reform whitepaper, and it marked data protection day in January 2026 ([whitepaper](2025-11-10-infocom-atia-reform-whitepaper), [day](2026-01-28-infocom-data-protection-day-2026)).

The same body holds both the access-to-information and the data-protection mandates, so the enforcement gap it identifies runs across both.

A regulator publishing that it cannot enforce its own orders is unusually direct, and it is the fact that governs how much weight the fully-in-force statute above can carry.

progress: Mixed, the corridor advanced elsewhere while the Seychelles memorandum stayed under review
summary: The country is one of seven covered by a [programme for African developing island economies](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch), on a 2026 to 2031 roadmap with digital transformation among six pillars.
developments:
The continental trade secretariat signed a joint venture in Accra on 31 August 2026 with the same technology company to establish the digital trade corridor ([agreement](2026-08-31-afcfta-quest-ghana-digital-trade-corridor)), while the Seychelles memorandum with the two remains under review. The corridor is proceeding through Ghana rather than through Seychelles.

The programme was launched at a ministerial segment in July 2026 ([programme](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch)).

No national commitment, allocation or workplan beyond the communique is detailed. It is the same seven-state programme recorded for other island units in this frame, and in none of them can the base say what the individual country undertook.

summary: A [digital-trade hub memorandum](2026-03-17-seychelles-nation-digital-trade-hub-afcfta) was signed with the continental trade secretariat and a technology partner, and its terms are not held.
developments:
The signing was reported during the secretary-general's visit in March 2026, positioning the country as a digital-trade hub ([memorandum](2026-03-17-seychelles-nation-digital-trade-hub-afcfta)).

A separate claim that a digital trade corridor headquarters sits in the capital is not established and is not conflated with the memorandum here.

No value, term, workplan or infrastructure commitment is published, so what a digital-trade hub would consist of is unstated.

summary: Parliament amended the broadcasting Act in June 2026 to give [appointment and dismissal power over the broadcaster board](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information), and [perceived media freedom](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information) fell on a survey round fielded in 2025.
developments:
The base holds no primary text of the amendment; it is reported in a survey dispatch citing two press-freedom organisations ([amendment](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information)).

The perception measure is from a round fielded in 2025 and published in August 2026. It measures what people believe about media freedom rather than the media's legal position, and an international index placed the country 35th globally in 2026, up ten places ([perception](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information)).

Those two point in opposite directions and the cell carries both: a statutory change increasing executive control over the state broadcaster, and an external ranking improving.

summary: A neighbouring operator [announced cross-border payment capabilities](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica) with a domestic fintech partner.
developments:
The announcement is a single paragraph in an otherwise foreign-focused keynote ([announcement](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

No agreement, value, timetable or regulatory approval is named. It is one of three cross-border payment intentions in this unit — the others being a continental interface memorandum and the domestic fintech's own platform — and none has a completed corridor on record.

summary: A [US$350,000 pre-seed round](2025-11-27-dabafinance-fusepay-preseed) closed for a domestic fintech, and a development lender [refinanced the telecommunications incumbent](2022-01-01-tdb-syc-cws-refinancing-2022-cable-wireless-seychelles-debt-refinancing-and) in a US$50m package after [arranging US$70m of acquisition financing](2019-01-01-tdb-syc-cws-acquisition-2019-cable-wireless-seychelles-acquisition-financing) in 2019.
developments:
The pre-seed closed in November 2025 with five named backers ([round](2025-11-27-dabafinance-fusepay-preseed)).

The refinancing package of US$50m replaced US$48.1m of 2019 debt ([refinancing](2022-01-01-tdb-syc-cws-refinancing-2022-cable-wireless-seychelles-debt-refinancing-and)); the lender took about 2.9 per cent of the operator's equity in December 2022, the operator listed on a domestic exchange in September 2022, and a local-currency bond of about US$12.5m was co-arranged in February 2024 ([refinancing](2022-01-01-tdb-syc-cws-refinancing-2022-cable-wireless-seychelles-debt-refinancing-and)).

The original acquisition financing of US$70m syndicated, US$50m on the lender's own book, took the operator out of foreign ownership in 2019 ([acquisition](2019-01-01-tdb-syc-cws-acquisition-2019-cable-wireless-seychelles-acquisition-financing)). A regional development lender holding equity in the telecommunications incumbent is a structural fact this base records and nothing examines.

summary: A [US$30m results-based social protection programme](2021-03-03 PAD - Seychelles Strengthening Quality of the Social Protection System PforR (PAD3541)) carries a social-protection registry and management information system as its digital element.
developments:
The programme was approved in March 2021 ([programme](2021-03-03 PAD - Seychelles Strengthening Quality of the Social Protection System PforR (PAD3541))).

It is the only development financing in this ledger with a named digital component, and the social protection delivery platform recorded separately — briefed to stakeholders in August 2026 — is presumably its output, though no source connects them.

summary: One operator [launched commercial fifth-generation service](2026-07-04-nation-airtel-seychelles-5g-launch-sbc) in July 2026, and the incumbent [launched fifth-generation with a Chinese vendor](2020-07-07-telecompaper-cable-wireless-seychelles-5g-huawei) in 2020.
developments:
The commercial launch came in July 2026 with a broadcaster content partnership alongside; plan and pricing detail is paywalled and not held ([launch](2026-07-04-nation-airtel-seychelles-5g-launch-sbc), [turnkey](2021-12-13-itweb-airtel-seychelles-ericsson-turnkey-5g)).

The incumbent launched fifth-generation service in 2020 with a Chinese vendor supplying it ([incumbent](2020-07-07-telecompaper-cable-wireless-seychelles-5g-huawei)).

An emergency-communications memorandum signed with a Chinese supplier at a 2025 trade congress, for a resilient mission-critical core integrating with the incumbent's network, has had no update in more than seventeen months ([memorandum](2025-03-04-developingtelecoms-hytera-cws-mou)).

summary: [Satellite internet soft-launched](2026-07-22-statehouse-seychelles-starlink-soft-launch) at a State House briefing in July 2026, after Cabinet approved the licence in February and the operator incorporated locally by May.
developments:
Cabinet approved the service provider licence on 18 February 2026, the operator incorporated locally and was in final licensing by May, and the soft launch was confirmed at a State House briefing in July ([soft launch](2026-07-22-statehouse-seychelles-starlink-soft-launch), [clearance](2026-03-06-nation-starlink-cleared-for-takeoff), [incorporation](2026-05-28-nation-starlink-incorporated-locally), [live](2026-07-20-starlink-live-cote-divoire-seychelles), [coverage](2026-07-28-starlink-adds-cote-divoire-and-seychelles-reaching-28-african-countries)).

Requiring local incorporation before licensing is the design choice worth recording: several units in this frame licensed the same operator on a full foreign-ownership basis, and this one did not.

No subscriber count, tariff or coverage figure is published.

summary: An [operator data centre](2021-12-13-itweb-airtel-seychelles-ericsson-turnkey-5g) was built under a turnkey project relocating and modernising the network into a hybrid network cloud.
developments:
The turnkey award was made in December 2021 ([project](2021-12-13-itweb-airtel-seychelles-ericsson-turnkey-5g)).

Its continued operation is inferred only from the 2026 fifth-generation launch it enabled. No capacity, tenancy or availability figure is published, and no other data centre — commercial or government — appears anywhere in this ledger.

summary: The National Assembly [unanimously approved a motion to accede to the Budapest Convention](2026-07-23-nation-sc-assembly-budapest-convention-accession), and a [national cybersecurity coordination committee](2025-05-13-nation-ai-nccc-amps-media) has a thin record with no founding instrument held.
developments:
The accession motion was approved unanimously in July 2026; the body of the source is paywalled beyond its opening ([accession](2026-07-23-nation-sc-assembly-budapest-convention-accession)).

The coordination committee reaches the base through a press-freedom day workshop it ran on artificial intelligence, ethics and cybersecurity. No founding instrument or mandate document is held ([committee](2025-05-13-nation-ai-nccc-amps-media)).

So the country is acceding to the principal international cybercrime instrument while its own coordinating body exists in the record only through a workshop it hosted.

summary: A [national digital identity platform](2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services) runs a two-tier credential built on a foreign vendor's platform, and no source addresses licensing, hosting or exit terms.
developments:
The platform launched in September 2024 on a foreign vendor's identity platform, with the credential made mandatory for work permit holders ([platform](2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services), [mandate](2024-09-18 Seychelles Makes Digital ID Mandatory for Work Permit Holders), [civil status](2022-11-01 Seychelles Civil Status Act Cap 34 (as at 1 Nov 2022))).

The sovereignty question is open: no source addresses licensing, hosting or exit terms with the vendor. For a national identity credential that is the arrangement that matters most, and it is the one thing nothing published says.

No enrolment count, coverage figure or authentication volume is held at any date.

summary: The central bank [set a four-stage cheque phase-out](2024-09-22 Seychelles to phase out cheques for financial transactions from 2025) running to May 2026, under [electronic money regulations](2022-12-12-seychelles-nps-electronic-money-regulations-2022) in force since 2022, and Cabinet [approved widening the authorised-dealer perimeter](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026).
developments:
The phase-out runs in four dated stages: stop issuing to individuals from January 2025, stop accepting from individuals from May 2025, stop issuing to non-residents from January 2026, stop accepting from non-residents after May 2026. The cheque-volume and card figures behind it carry a proxy date caveat ([phase-out](2024-09-22 Seychelles to phase out cheques for financial transactions from 2025), [schedule](2026-07-09-nation-src-cheque-phaseout-2028)).

The electronic money regulations were made under the payment system Act in 2022, giving incumbents six months to comply and a year to reach the capital floor; they were acquired from the Official Gazette only in August 2026, so they are a foundational text newly added to this base rather than a new development ([regulations](2022-12-12-seychelles-nps-electronic-money-regulations-2022)).

Cabinet approved amendments widening the authorised-dealer definition to include credit unions and licensed payment service providers ([perimeter](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026)). A dated, staged withdrawal of an instrument is the most orderly payments transition in this frame.

summary: A [domestic fintech ran its first live transaction](2026-07-22-fusepay-fuse360-ai-operating-system) on a virtual business-account platform, positioned against the cheque phase-out.
developments:
The first live transaction ran in July 2026 on a platform offering virtual business accounts, with the company also announcing an operating layer above it ([platform](2026-07-22-fusepay-fuse360-ai-operating-system), [cheques](2025-11-21-techafricanews-fusepay-cheques), [funding](2025-11-27-dabafinance-fusepay-preseed)).

A domestic company building business payments directly into the gap the central bank's cheque withdrawal creates is the clearest instance in this ledger of policy and private delivery lining up.

No transaction volume, customer count or pricing is published.

summary: The central bank [signed a memorandum with an Indian payments body](2026-06-30-africabusinessinsight-seychelles-upi) to bring its unified payments interface, with rollout targeted for end-2026.
developments:
The memorandum was signed during a bilateral visit in June 2026 and the source is secondary, with neither party's primary held ([memorandum](2026-06-30-africabusinessinsight-seychelles-upi)).

Adopting another country's national payments interface is a substantial architectural commitment — it decides the rails, the standards and the counterparty for cross-border retail payments — and the base holds no text stating what was agreed.

summary: [Civil-status certificates are issued online](2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services) with two-working-day delivery, saved to the identity platform's document wallet.
developments:
Birth, marriage and death certificates are available online with delivery in two working days, saved into the identity platform's document wallet ([certificates](2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services)).

That is a working registry-to-credential link — the certificate lands in the same wallet as the identity — and it is one of very few in this frame where the two systems are joined at the point of issue.

No transaction volume, registration completeness or uptake figure is published.

summary: Cabinet approved implementation of a [national addressing and postcode system](2025-01-01 National Addressing System - Seychelles Postal Regulator) on an international address standard, with the legal framework being drafted.
developments:
The standard was adopted and a technical committee is drafting the legal framework with the attorney-general's office ([system](2025-01-01 National Addressing System - Seychelles Postal Regulator)).

The source is undated and proxy-dated to 2025, so the status may have moved with nothing later on record. Adopting the international standard before drafting the law is the sequence here, and it is the right one for an addressing system whose value depends on conforming to something.

summary: The President [toured the registrar general office](2025-02-10 Seychelles Pledges to Modernize Public Services Through Digital Transformation), praised its digitalisation and announced unspecified legislative reforms.
developments:
The tour was in February 2025 and the reforms were not specified ([tour](2025-02-10 Seychelles Pledges to Modernize Public Services Through Digital Transformation)).

Nothing has entered the base since. A business one-stop portal was separately launched in pilot with a full rollout targeted for June 2026, and no source connects it to the registry.

summary: [Bilateral consultations are advancing](2026-08-08-india-tech-sovereignty-push-africa-asean) toward potential adoption of another country's telemedicine, office and hospital platforms.
developments:
The consultations reach the base through a single secondary analytical source, with no domestic primary ([consultations](2026-08-08-india-tech-sovereignty-push-africa-asean)).

Adopting a foreign state's public-health platforms alongside a memorandum to adopt its payments interface would make one bilateral partner the supplier of two of this country's core public systems. Nothing published states terms, hosting or data arrangements for either.

summary: A [smart education programme](2025-08-30-huawei-smart-education-seychelles) was launched by the education ministry with the incumbent operator and a Chinese vendor across four secondary schools.
developments:
The programme covers multimedia lessons, real-time assessment and interactive display hardware across four secondary schools ([programme](2025-08-30-huawei-smart-education-seychelles)).

The account is a vendor case study, not verified against a ministry primary. No pupil count, evaluation or data arrangement is published, and the same vendor supplies the incumbent's fifth-generation core.

summary: An [electronic case management system](2026-06-23-statehouse-ecms-launch) was launched by the President in June 2026, live with immediate effect.
developments:
It went live on launch ([system](2026-06-23-statehouse-ecms-launch)).

No court coverage, case volume, filing arrangement or public-access provision is published. It is one of four government systems this unit brought into service inside four weeks in mid-2026, alongside the portal relaunch, the certificate of origin and the fifth-generation launch.

summary: [Mandatory electronic invoicing](2026-07-25-seychelles-src-final-stage-e-invoicing-procurement) is at the final stage of procurement, on an expression of interest opened in March 2026.
developments:
The acting commissioner general stated in July 2026 that the expression of interest opened in March and procurement is at final stage ([procurement](2026-07-25-seychelles-src-final-stage-e-invoicing-procurement)).

No supplier, value, mandate date or taxpayer scope is published. Making invoicing mandatory is the point at which a revenue digitisation reaches every business in the country, and none of the terms on which it will do so is on record.

summary: The revenue commission [launched an electronic certificate of origin](2026-07-04-comesa-seychelles-eco-launch) with the regional trade secretariat.
developments:
It was launched in July 2026 for trade facilitation ([certificate](2026-07-04-comesa-seychelles-eco-launch)).

No issuance volume, participating trader count or processing-time figure is published. It is the operational half of the digital-trade hub positioning recorded separately, and the only part of it that has actually been delivered.

summary: The [government portal was relaunched](2026-06-24-techafricanews-egov-portal) in June 2026, a [business one-stop portal](2025-11-07-nrd-seychelles-eodb-portal) entered pilot with fifteen or more services, and a [social protection delivery platform](2026-08-18-nation-sc-asp-connect-social-protection-platform) was briefed to stakeholders.
developments:
The portal relaunch coincided with the fiftieth independence anniversary ([portal](2026-06-24-techafricanews-egov-portal)).

The business portal launched with a vendor in November 2025 covering two service journeys and fifteen or more services, with full rollout targeted for June 2026; the account is a vendor press release not verified against a ministry primary ([business](2025-11-07-nrd-seychelles-eodb-portal)).

The social protection platform was briefed rather than launched in August 2026, with no go-live date, beneficiary count or service list published ([platform](2026-08-18-nation-sc-asp-connect-social-protection-platform)). Against a 2030 target of full digitalisation, no source states how many services exist or how many are online.

summary: An [eight-week video-enforcement pilot](2026-07-30-seychelles-video-enforcement-traffic-system) repurposes the public camera estate for automated offence detection and remote ticketing, with no data-protection basis stated.
developments:
The pilot was announced in July 2026 with a foreign technology partner ([pilot](2026-07-30-seychelles-video-enforcement-traffic-system)).

No data-protection basis is stated on record. That matters more here than in most units, because the country's data protection Act is fully in force and its regulator has published that it has no clear power to enforce its orders — so the safeguard exists in statute and not in practice.

Repurposing an existing camera estate for automated enforcement is a change of purpose for data already collected, which is exactly the kind of processing the Act would govern.

summary: Cabinet approved a [National AI in Education Framework 2026-2030](2026-07-31-seychelles-national-ai-in-education-framework-2026-2030) covering every state school, with a mandatory teacher micro-credential and per-school champions, and two [artificial-intelligence tutoring and coaching pilots](2026-07-31-seychelles-national-ai-in-education-framework-2026-2030) are running.
developments:
The 21-page policy covers every state school, artificial-intelligence literacy across the curriculum, a mandatory micro-credential for teachers, a champion in each school, and a steering committee maintaining approved and prohibited tool lists ([framework](2026-07-31-seychelles-national-ai-in-education-framework-2026-2030), [cabinet](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026)).

Implementation timeline, budget, indicators and tool-approval criteria are unestablished, and an automated attempt to acquire the document failed.

A student tutoring pilot covers secondary mathematics and geography ([tutor](2026-07-31-seychelles-national-ai-in-education-framework-2026-2030)) and a teacher coaching pilot covers lesson planning and classroom practice for upper primary ([coach](2026-07-31-seychelles-national-ai-in-education-framework-2026-2030)); neither pilot's start date is given. A steering committee maintaining a prohibited-tools list is a governance design few units in this frame have attempted.

summary: [Public support for access to government information](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information) was measured in a survey round fielded in 2025 and published in August 2026.
developments:
It is the only measure of public opinion on information access in this ledger ([support](2026-08-11-seychelles-afrobarometer-media-oversight-access-information)).

It arrives in the same dispatch as the media-freedom perception measure and the report of the broadcasting amendment, so a single external survey is carrying the whole of this unit's civic-participation record.

summary: Cabinet approved measures [operationalising a multidimensional vulnerability index](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026), naming enhanced data and institutional capacity as the instruments, and an [island states resilience data programme](2026-08-19-nation-sc-res-islands-seychelles-launch) launched nationally.
developments:
The Cabinet measures name enhanced data and institutional capacity and the alignment of planning and budgeting frameworks as the instruments for operationalising the index ([index](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026)).

The resilience data programme was launched nationally in August 2026; the grant figure attached to it covers a nine-country programme and the national share is not published ([programme](2026-08-19-nation-sc-res-islands-seychelles-launch), [launch](2026-08-18-uneca-resislands-seychelles-national-launch)).

Both are about building the data on which small-island vulnerability is measured, which for this country is the statistical question with the most policy weight attached to it.

summary: Cabinet approved [accession to the United Nations outer space committee](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026), framed as building geospatial capability for maritime security, disaster preparedness and ocean management.
developments:
The approval came in July 2026 ([accession](2026-07-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-july-2026)).

No programme, data source, budget or partner is named. For an ocean state whose exclusive economic zone dwarfs its land area, geospatial capability for maritime security and ocean management is the substantive case, and accession to a committee is the first step rather than the capability.

summary: A [Chinese vendor supplies the incumbent fifth-generation core](2020-07-07-telecompaper-cable-wireless-seychelles-5g-huawei) and, with the education ministry, the [smart education programme](2025-08-30-huawei-smart-education-seychelles) across four schools.
developments:
The vendor supplied the incumbent's fifth-generation launch in 2020 and the school programme in August 2025 ([core](2020-07-07-telecompaper-cable-wireless-seychelles-5g-huawei), [schools](2025-08-30-huawei-smart-education-seychelles)).

A second Chinese supplier holds the stalled emergency-communications memorandum with the same incumbent, unmoved in more than seventeen months.

So Chinese vendors supply the mobile core, a school technology programme and a proposed emergency-communications core, and no procurement terms, security review or exit arrangement is published for any of them.

summary: The [National ICT Policy](2007-01-01-seychelles-national-ict-policy) of 2007 is still the standing whole-of-government instrument, with no successor, revision or evaluation held.
developments:
The policy covers ICT infrastructure, the legal and regulatory framework, human resources, industry and government ([policy](2007-01-01-seychelles-national-ict-policy)); the document carries no date on its face and 2007 comes from a third-party policy portal.

Delivery has continued without it: the official citizen portal was relaunched in June 2026, timed to the fiftieth anniversary of independence ([portal](2026-06-23-nation-sc-revamped-govsc-portal)).

Nineteen years on, nothing held records the policy being reviewed, costed or replaced, so what governs ICT strategy is an instrument older than the smartphone.

summary: There is no standalone national broadband strategy; the closest instrument is the regulator's [revised wireless-access spectrum policy](2025-01-22-seychelles-fbwa-policy-revised) of 2025.
developments:
The revised policy governs licence-exempt use of the 2.4 and 5.8 GHz bands for fixed broadband wireless access, superseding the 2004 policy ([policy](2025-01-22-seychelles-fbwa-policy-revised)).

The connectivity targets a broadband strategy would carry sit instead in the universal access and universal service provisions of the [Communications Act 2023](2023-04-13-gazette-communications-act-2023), and nothing held sets a coverage or speed target under either.

summary: No whole-of-government cloud strategy exists; a [spatial data sharing policy](2020-01-01-seychelles-spatial-data-sharing-policy) provides for distributed hosting, and a Tier IV data centre opened in 2026.
developments:
The 2020 policy adopts international geospatial principles and provides for distributed data-centre hosting and for OGC and ISO interoperability standards across ministries; it is sectoral, not a whole-of-government instrument ([policy](2020-01-01-seychelles-spatial-data-sharing-policy)).

The country's first Tier IV certified data centre opened at Anse Boileau in March 2026, positioned by its operator as keeping government services and financial institutions onshore rather than on overseas facilities ([data centre](2026-03-20-cable-wireless-seychelles-linkedin-tier-iv-data-centre)).

So the capacity arrived before the policy: nothing held states where government workloads are to run, or on what terms.

summary: No whole-of-government interoperability framework is held; the [spatial data sharing policy](2020-01-01-seychelles-spatial-data-sharing-policy) and the ICT department's standards mandate are the nearest instruments.
developments:
The 2020 spatial policy provides for OGC and ISO interoperability standards across ministries within its own domain ([policy](2020-01-01-seychelles-spatial-data-sharing-policy)).

The ICT department states that adopted technical standards for the seamless interoperability of e-government services, and the integration of every e-government application and database, fall within its Policy, Standards and Research Section's mandate ([mandate](2026-09-01-dict-policy-standards-research-section)); the standards themselves are not published.

What is held is a sectoral policy and a departmental mandate, and no roadmap, target architecture or sequencing plan behind either.

summary: No standalone national data-governance policy exists; the [National Bureau of Statistics Act 2010](2010-07-09-seychelles-national-bureau-of-statistics-act-2010) is the closest institutional instrument.
developments:
The Act, assented on 9 July 2010, founds the Bureau and the national statistical system and repeals the 2005 statute ([Act](2010-07-09-seychelles-national-bureau-of-statistics-act-2010)).

The African Union's peer review of May 2025 records the Bureau's professional independence and recommends a new Statistics Bill ([review](2025-10-17-statafric-seychelles-peer-review-report)), which is the nearest thing on record to a legislative data-governance reform.

Data governance is otherwise distributed across the Data Protection Act, the statistics statute and a sectoral spatial policy, with no instrument tying them together.

summary: There is [no open government data policy](2020-09-10-eiti-seychelles-board-decision-2020-67); a 2020 corrective action to publish one is not shown closed.
developments:
The extractives transparency board found in September 2020 that revenue data was published in open format but that the multi-stakeholder group did not appear to have an open data policy, and set a corrective-action deadline to publish one ([decision](2020-09-10-eiti-seychelles-board-decision-2020-67)).

Nothing held records that policy being made. In December 2025 the statistics bureau opened two externally financed expressions of interest to modernise its website and improve public access to national data ([procurement](2025-12-05-nation-sc-nbs-website-modernisation-eois)) — a procurement step, not a portal and not a policy.

summary: The [Cybercrimes Act 2021](2021-12-15-seychelles-cybercrimes-and-other-related-crimes-act-2021) was [amended in December 2025](2025-12-22-seychelles-cybercrimes-amendment-act-2025), widening offences and adding search and interception powers.
developments:
The 2021 Act created the first standalone cybercrime offences regime, repealing the Computer Misuse Act, and commenced on 1 February 2022 ([Act](2021-12-15-seychelles-cybercrimes-and-other-related-crimes-act-2021)).

The amendment passed the National Assembly on 15 December and was assented on 22 December 2025; it widens the offence definitions, defines subscriber information as identity, address and billing or service details, and adds search and interception powers ([amendment](2025-12-22-seychelles-cybercrimes-amendment-act-2025)).

Cabinet separately approved a judiciary digitalisation programme in May 2026 expressly requiring stronger cybersecurity and data-management systems around the courts ([judiciary](2026-05-14-statehouse-seychelles-cabinet-business-13-may-judiciary-digitalization)). No prosecution, caseload or enforcement figure under the Act is published.

summary: The identity-card statute was [amended in 2023](2023-11-08-seychelles-miscellaneous-amendments-act-2023) on identity numbers and disclosure; no statute names or governs the SeyID credential itself.
developments:
Part 13 of the 2023 omnibus Act amends the National Identity Cards Act on the national identity number requirement, cards for non-resident citizens and the rules on disclosing information, and does not create the digital credential ([Act](2023-11-08-seychelles-miscellaneous-amendments-act-2023)).

The December 2025 cybercrimes amendment defines subscriber information — identity, address and billing or service details — for evidential purposes, the strongest in-window legal movement touching identity data ([amendment](2025-12-22-seychelles-cybercrimes-amendment-act-2025)).

So the physical card has a statute and the digital credential has none: SeyID rests on administrative practice, which is a different kind of guarantee.

summary: The [National Payment System Act 2014](2014-08-18-seylii-national-payment-system-act-2014) is the statute, and [December 2025 regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025) made interoperable IT systems a licence condition.
developments:
Act 14 of 2014 commenced on 18 August 2014 and has been amended by the 2022 electronic money regulations and a 2023 amendment Act ([Act](2014-08-18-seylii-national-payment-system-act-2014)).

The amendment to the licensing and authorisation regulations, made on 15 December 2025, requires safe and reliable IT systems and adequate interfaces to ensure straight-through processing as a condition of licence for payment, clearing and settlement operators ([regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025)).

Cabinet approved amendments to the Foreign Exchange Act in July 2026 adding credit unions and payment service providers to the class of authorised dealers ([Cabinet](2026-07-24-nation-sc-cabinet-clears-major-reforms)); that approval is not yet an enacted instrument.

summary: The [payment licensing regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025) make straight-through processing a licence condition; a National Addressing System Bill was Cabinet-approved in April 2026.
developments:
The December 2025 regulations require payment, clearing and settlement operators to hold safe and reliable IT systems and adequate interfaces for straight-through processing, the clearest statutory interoperability duty the base holds ([regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025)).

Cabinet approved the National Addressing System Bill in April 2026, creating a National Addressing Department and Database Unit as a shared reference-data layer described as improving cross-agency access to data ([Bill](2026-04-03-seychelles-national-addressing-system-bill-cabinet)).

Both are sectoral. No general statute obliges public bodies to share or expose data to one another, and the addressing Bill is approved rather than enacted.

summary: The [Broadcasting Corporation Act 2026](2026-07-13-seychelles-broadcasting-corporation-act-2026) requires an AI-use policy for content and broadcast operations — the only statutory AI duty held.
developments:
The Act, assented on 9 July and gazetted on 13 July 2026, repeals the 2011 statute and requires the Corporation to develop and periodically review a policy on the use of artificial intelligence in content creation, curation and broadcast operations ([Act](2026-07-13-seychelles-broadcasting-corporation-act-2026)).

It is sector-specific and applies to one state broadcaster. No general artificial-intelligence statute, regulation or code applies across the economy, and the policy the Act requires is not itself held.

summary: The [Electronic Transactions Act 2001](2001-01-01-seychelles-electronic-transactions-act-2001) gives legal effect to electronic records and digital signatures; customs payment rules were digitised in 2026.
developments:
The founding statute recognises electronic records, digital signatures and electronic dealings with public authorities; the consolidated text held is current to 29 March 2018 ([Act](2001-01-01-seychelles-electronic-transactions-act-2001)), and a 2024 statutory instrument amending its exclusions schedule is not applied to it.

In April 2026 Cabinet approved customs regulations requiring electronic or bank-transfer payment of dues of R50,000 and above and operationalising the ATA Carnet system ([Cabinet](2026-04-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-april-2026)).

The statute is twenty-five years old and has not been revisited for platforms, marketplaces or consumer contracting online.

summary: The [National Bureau of Statistics Act 2010](2010-07-09-seychelles-national-bureau-of-statistics-act-2010) is in force, and the African Union's 2025 peer review recommends replacing it.
developments:
The Act was assented on 9 July 2010, founding the Bureau and the national statistical system and repealing the 2005 statute ([Act](2010-07-09-seychelles-national-bureau-of-statistics-act-2010)).

The peer review conducted in May 2025 and published in October records the Bureau's professional independence and recommends a new Statistics Bill ([review](2025-10-17-statafric-seychelles-peer-review-report)); nothing held records one being drafted.

The census the Bureau ran in 2022 was conducted under a separate Census Act, itself revised by the 2023 omnibus amendments ([amendments](2023-11-08-seychelles-miscellaneous-amendments-act-2023)).

summary: Seychelles is a founding party to the [SADC Treaty](2026-08-01-sadc-consolidated-treaty-2025), whose Protocol mechanism is the route to regional legal harmonisation.
developments:
The consolidated 2025 edition of the Treaty names Seychelles among the founding High Contracting Parties and sets out the Community's institutions, areas of co-operation and the Protocol mechanism ([treaty](2026-08-01-sadc-consolidated-treaty-2025)).

No ratification instrument for any specific digital or data protocol is held, so what can be established is membership of the framework rather than adoption of anything harmonised through it.

summary: The African Union [urged AfCFTA parties](2026-02-15-au-assembly-dec956-afcfta-activity-report) to operationalise cross-border data commitments; an [EU agreement](2026-06-10-ec-eu-esa4-enhanced-epa-factsheet) would bar unjustified localisation.
developments:
The Assembly's 39th Ordinary Session in February 2026 urged State Parties to operationalise digital public infrastructure commitments on cross-border data protection and transfers under the Protocol on Digital Trade ([decision](2026-02-15-au-assembly-dec956-afcfta-activity-report)).

In June 2026 the European Union and four eastern and southern African states including Seychelles concluded negotiations on an enhanced Economic Partnership Agreement carrying a binding prohibition of unjustified data-localisation requirements and a permanent ban on customs duties on electronic transmissions ([agreement](2026-06-10-ec-eu-esa4-enhanced-epa-factsheet)).

Domestically, the Data Protection Act 2023's cross-border transfer conditions are the operative rule ([regulator](2026-02-06-infocom-seychelles-data-protection-page)). Nothing records a transfer authorised, refused or notified under it.

summary: The [Seychelles Bureau of Standards](2014-03-31-seychelles-bureau-of-standards-act-2014-full-text) gained a new board from August 2025 and [accredited mass-calibration capability](2025-09-15-sadcas-seychelles-mass-calibration-accreditation) in September.
developments:
The Bureau is constituted under Act 2 of 2014, commenced in June 2014 and amended in 2016 and 2021, whose 36 sections set the Board, the standards-making procedure, offences and penalties ([Act](2014-03-31-seychelles-bureau-of-standards-act-2014-full-text)).

A new eight-member Board was appointed for three years with effect from 1 August 2025 ([gazette](2025-09-29-gazette-64-sbs-board-appointment)), and the regional accreditation service's register shows the Bureau's mass-calibration capability approved on 15 September 2025 and valid to 14 September 2030 ([register](2025-09-15-sadcas-seychelles-mass-calibration-accreditation)).

No count of national standards adopted, and no annual report of the Bureau, is held.

summary: The ICT department [claims the mandate](2026-09-01-dict-policy-standards-research-section) for government-wide interoperability standards; the standards themselves are not published.
developments:
The department states that adopted technical standards intended to support the seamless interoperability of e-government services, and the integration of all e-government applications and databases through established software and database standards, fall within its Policy, Standards and Research Section ([mandate](2026-09-01-dict-policy-standards-research-section)).

Nothing held names a standard, a version or a conformance route. The nearest published interoperability requirement is sectoral: the December 2025 payment regulations obliging straight-through processing ([regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025)).

summary: Seychelles moved all domestic and cross-border electronic payments to [ISO 20022](2025-04-14-cbs-sba-iso-20022-transition-notice) from 22 November 2025, replacing SWIFT MT formats.
developments:
The central bank and the bankers' association jointly notified the adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging standard for all domestic and cross-border electronic payments, replacing SWIFT MT formats, with effect from 22 November 2025 ([notice](2025-04-14-cbs-sba-iso-20022-transition-notice)).

In the standards infrastructure proper, the Bureau of Standards gained externally accredited mass-calibration capability in September 2025 ([accreditation](2025-09-15-sadcas-seychelles-mass-calibration-accreditation)).

No completion statement or migration report after the November effective date is held, so the adoption is dated by its deadline rather than by its delivery.

summary: Industry answered the [virtual-asset licensing consultation](2024-03-07-seychelles-vasp-framework-industry-consultation-response) with about fifteen written responses, and banks fed a [cybersecurity baseline](2025-10-17-nccc-sba-cybersecurity-workshop) in 2025.
developments:
The regulator's formal consultation response of March 2024 records about fifteen written responses and fifty to sixty live participants on the licensing framework ([response](2024-03-07-seychelles-vasp-framework-industry-consultation-response)); it is the fullest dated record of private-sector input to a digital or data policy process the base holds.

In October 2025 the cybersecurity coordination committee and the bankers' association ran a joint workshop introducing a National Cybersecurity Baseline, with a member bank presenting a case study ([workshop](2025-10-17-nccc-sba-cybersecurity-workshop)).

In July 2026 the Vice-President agreed to involve the university in the consultation and planning stages of national digitalisation and AI initiatives ([university](2026-07-16-unisey-vice-president-strategic-partnership)).

summary: The [2026 appropriation](2026-03-30-gazette-appropriation-act-2026) gives the ICT department R93.813 million of R11.84 billion — an annual departmental line, not a dedicated fund.
developments:
The Appropriation Act 2026 authorises R11,842,682,521 of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund and appropriates R93.813 million to the Department of Information Communications Technology ([Act](2026-03-30-gazette-appropriation-act-2026)); it was passed on 13 March, assented on 23 March and gazetted on 30 March 2026.

The National Assembly Administration Act 2026 creates an autonomous Parliamentary Service with its own Office of Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Data Security at section 16, a Parliamentary Budget Office, and financial-autonomy provisions putting appropriations and retained underspend under the Commission ([Act](2026-06-15-gazette-national-assembly-administration-act-2026)).

The appropriation gives one departmental figure and no programme breakdown, so what the rest of government spends on digital transformation is not established.

summary: [87.8 per cent of the population used the internet in 2024](2026-04-14-fred-internet-users-seychelles), against 79.3 per cent in 2020; a tracker puts [16,800 people still offline](2025-11-08-datareportal-digital-2026-seychelles).
developments:
The World Bank and ITU series puts internet use at 87.818 per cent of the population in 2024, against 79.3 per cent in 2020 ([series](2026-04-14-fred-internet-users-seychelles)).

A commercial tracker dated October 2025 puts 117,000 users, 87.4 per cent penetration and an estimated 16,800 people, or 12.6 per cent, still offline ([tracker](2025-11-08-datareportal-digital-2026-seychelles)).

The two are close but differently constructed. No national survey of who is offline and why is held, so the residual has a size and no description.

summary: The World Bank finds [internet cost a barrier to inclusion](2024-06-25-worldbank-seychelles-cpf-fy25-30); Cabinet [reformed prepaid and e-SIM rules](2026-03-19-statehouse-cabinet-business-prepaid-esim) in March 2026.
developments:
The lender's country partnership framework states that despite high mobile coverage and broadband subscription rates, the cost of internet remains a barrier to greater digital inclusivity ([framework](2024-06-25-worldbank-seychelles-cpf-fy25-30)).

In March 2026 Cabinet approved amendments to the prepaid mobile regulations allowing e-SIM sales through digital platforms, requiring annual operator audits and capping tourist and non-resident SIMs at 21 days ([Cabinet](2026-03-19-statehouse-cabinet-business-prepaid-esim)); the changes modernise compliance rather than tariffs.

Operators have competed on volume instead: entry-level unlimited fibre plans rose to a minimum 60 Mbps at no extra cost in April 2026 ([upgrade](2026-04-02-linkedin-cws-fibre-broadband-upgrade)). No tariff basket or price-per-gigabyte series for Seychelles is held.

summary: The incumbent [upgraded its national fibre network to 50G-PON](2026-04-02-linkedin-cws-fibre-broadband-upgrade) in April 2026, raising entry-level unlimited plans to 60 Mbps at no extra cost.
developments:
The upgrade raised entry-level unlimited plans to a minimum of 60 Mbps and capped plans to a minimum 30 GB automatically, on newly deployed 50G-PON technology across the fibre network ([upgrade](2026-04-02-linkedin-cws-fibre-broadband-upgrade)).

The competing operator had launched unlimited home broadband from R999 for 10 Mbps in September 2025, with a R200 booster to 200 Mbps ([package](2025-09-13-nation-sc-airtel-smart-connect)).

Both announcements are the operators' own. Neither publishes homes passed, subscriber numbers or coverage by district, and the regulator's quarterly statistics carry no fibre series.

summary: International bandwidth stood at [308,074 Mbps at 31 March 2026](2026-06-01-scra-ict-q1-2026-statistics), unchanged on the quarter, against 17,870 Mbps in March 2020.
developments:
The regulator's first-quarter 2026 statistics give national international internet bandwidth of 308,074 Mbps, 154,023 uplink and 154,051 downlink, unchanged from the fourth quarter of 2025, against 17,870 Mbps at the start of the published series in March 2020 ([statistics](2026-06-01-scra-ict-q1-2026-statistics)).

The capacity behind it is two submarine cables: the SEAS link, and the PEACE cable in service since 16 November 2022 ([cables](2023-01-06-nation-sc-peace-operational-seychelles)). No utilisation figure against the lit capacity is published.

summary: An [internet exchange point was launched in February 2015](2015-02-20-au-int-ixp-launch-seychelles) under the African Union's AXIS project; nothing since records its operating state.
developments:
The African Union's own launch statement records the exchange point established with the Department of ICT to keep intra-country internet traffic inside the country ([launch](2015-02-20-au-int-ixp-launch-seychelles)).

Eleven years on, no peering count, traffic figure, member list or operating statement is held, and nothing more current than the launch announcement was found. What the base establishes is that an exchange point was created, not that one runs.

summary: A [Tier III data centre at Perseverance](2022-01-04-sbc-airtel-perseverance-data-centre) offers colocation and customer disaster recovery — the only off-site backup capacity the base records.
developments:
The facility is described by its operator as carrying redundant power and cooling and serving customer disaster-recovery planning with round-the-clock monitoring ([data centre](2022-01-04-sbc-airtel-perseverance-data-centre)).

A second, Tier IV certified facility opened at Anse Boileau in March 2026, positioned as keeping government and financial-institution systems onshore ([Tier IV](2026-03-20-cable-wireless-seychelles-linkedin-tier-iv-data-centre)).

Nothing held states where government data is actually backed up, whether any ministry holds an off-site copy, or what recovery objectives apply.

summary: The [first Tier IV certified data centre](2025-09-04-uptime-institute-bon-espoir-certification) was certified in September 2025 and opened in March 2026, beside an existing Tier III facility.
developments:
The certifying body's record names Cable and Wireless (Seychelles) Limited as client and Data Center 1 at Bon Espoir, Anse Boileau, as the certified facility, with a Tier IV construction and design award issued on 4 September 2025 and valid to 2027 ([certification](2025-09-04-uptime-institute-bon-espoir-certification)).

The operator announced the opening in March 2026 as the country's first Tier IV data centre, positioned to keep government services and financial institutions onshore rather than dependent on overseas facilities ([opening](2026-03-20-cable-wireless-seychelles-linkedin-tier-iv-data-centre)).

No floor area, rack count, power capacity or customer list is published for either facility.

summary: The utility reports [99.5 per cent electricity coverage and 45,364 customers](2024-01-01-puc-2023-annual-report), with a network project cutting South Mahé losses from about 16 to 6 per cent.
developments:
The 2023 operator report gives 99.5 per cent coverage, 45,364 customers, generating assets at Roche Caiman 77.5 MW, New Port 28.75 MW, Baie Ste Anne 15.39 MW and La Digue 2.46 MW, a South Mahé 33 kV project cutting network losses from about 16 per cent to 6 per cent, and 20 MWp of renewable capacity ([report](2024-01-01-puc-2023-annual-report)).

The 2024 report holds coverage at 99.5 per cent with 1,279 employees and renewables at 4.2 per cent of supply ([report](2025-05-30-puc-2024-annual-report)).

No outage-duration or interruption-frequency series is published, so reliability is described by coverage and losses rather than measured by downtime.

summary: Coverage is [99.5 per cent](2025-05-30-puc-2024-annual-report); a [renewable acceleration programme](2026-03-05-worldbank-reap-isr-p505856) became effective in February 2026 with every target still at zero.
developments:
The utility reports 99.5 per cent electricity coverage across the islands ([report](2025-05-30-puc-2024-annual-report)), which leaves little rural electrification to do in the ordinary sense.

The Renewable Energy Acceleration Program became effective on 26 February 2026 with the utility advancing procurement; its targets of 18 MW of renewable capacity, 18 MWh of storage enabled, a 7 per cent average reduction in outage duration and 500 grid-connected businesses benefiting by May 2030 all stood at zero at 28 February 2026 ([status](2026-03-05-worldbank-reap-isr-p505856)).

What is left to solve here is generation mix and reliability rather than reach.

summary: The World Bank records that Seychelles [meets only 60 per cent of its residents' water requirements](2024-06-25-worldbank-seychelles-cpf-fy25-30), with demand rising 7 to 8 per cent a year.
developments:
The lender's country partnership framework states that Seychelles can meet only 60 per cent of its residents' water requirements against demand rising 7 to 8 per cent a year ([framework](2024-06-25-worldbank-seychelles-cpf-fy25-30)).

On the power side the utility reports 99.5 per cent coverage and renewables at 4.2 per cent of supply ([report](2025-05-30-puc-2024-annual-report)), with a renewable acceleration programme effective from February 2026 ([programme](2026-03-05-worldbank-reap-isr-p505856)).

Nothing held connects either constraint to the two data centres now operating, so the question of whether the supply is sufficient for them has no dated answer.

summary: The [2019-2024 cybersecurity strategy](2019-01-01-ict-gov-sc-national-cybersecurity-strategy) made ministry security audits mandatory; its period has expired and no successor is held.
developments:
The department's founding strategy sets the CERT-SC and Cybersecurity Unit governance structure, mandatory information-security auditing of ministries, departments and agencies, and a 2019-2024 action plan for protecting government ICT infrastructure ([strategy](2019-01-01-ict-gov-sc-national-cybersecurity-strategy)).

The department runs the Electronic Government Network that ministries and district administrations connect to, and the SeyID platform, with 74 staff ([department](2025-06-17-national-assembly-dict-egn-visit)).

No audit result, incident figure or evaluation against the action plan is published, and the strategy's own period ended two years ago with nothing recorded to replace it.

summary: A [three-year Indian programme to train 250 civil servants](2026-05-12-ncgg-pib-seychelles-capacity-building-cohort) began in May 2026; the ICT department runs the government network with 74 staff.
developments:
The first cohort of 29 officials — from information technology, the judiciary, education and other senior posts — began on 11 May 2026 under a three-year agreement to train 250 Seychellois civil servants, covering digital public infrastructure, electronic courts and AI-enabled governance ([cohort](2026-05-12-ncgg-pib-seychelles-capacity-building-cohort)), and completed a two-week programme on 22 May ([completion](2026-06-10-nationalassembly-first-capacity-building-programme)).

The ICT department administers and expands the Electronic Government Network with 74 staff ([department](2025-06-17-national-assembly-dict-egn-visit)), and the national strategy for 2024-2028 puts a modern public service as its first priority area ([strategy](2024-01-01-seychelles-national-development-strategy-2024-2028)).

No establishment figure, vacancy rate or turnover statistic for government ICT posts is published.

summary: There is no national data exchange layer; [India committed to building Seychelles' digital public infrastructure](2026-02-09-india-seychelles-sesel-joint-vision) in February 2026.
developments:
The February 2026 joint vision records India undertaking comprehensive efforts on the build-out of Seychelles' digital public infrastructure, including digital payments ([vision](2026-02-09-india-seychelles-sesel-joint-vision)), with a Digital Transformation memorandum between the two ICT ministries signed the same day ([memorandum](2026-02-10-statehouse-seychelles-india-175m-package-mous)).

Domestically the nearest step is Cabinet's April 2026 approval of a National Addressing System Bill creating a shared reference-data layer described as improving cross-agency access to data ([Bill](2026-04-03-seychelles-national-addressing-system-bill-cabinet)).

What exists is a commitment and a reference register. No exchange layer, no registry of connected systems and no transaction volume is held.

summary: The digital identity now gates [licensing services on monServis](2023-04-19-sla-online-services-seyid-monservis) and the [social protection platform](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch) launched in October 2025.
developments:
The licensing authority's business and vehicle licence services moved to monServis and require SeyID authentication, the former gateway being obsolete ([licensing](2023-04-19-sla-online-services-seyid-monservis)).

The social protection agency's platform, launched internally on 15 October 2025, is reached through the SeyID portal that hosts government-entity systems ([platform](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch)), and in March 2026 Cabinet extended its vendor support and directed the ICT department to lead the transition to government ownership ([Cabinet](2026-03-05-asp-connect-cabinet-stabilisation)).

The wallet also carries a Digital Driving Licence connected live to the licensing authority's own system ([wallet](2026-01-01-seyid-idwallet)). No authentication volume is published.

summary: Health data capture is [primarily paper-based](2022-01-01-seychelles-nhsp-strategic-direction-six-data) with the electronic system stalled; a [July 2026 reform](2026-07-21-nation-sc-new-era-of-care) makes digital health a pillar.
developments:
The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 records that data capture is primarily paper-based, that implementation of an electronic health information system begun in 2020 had stalled, and that no formal data-governance standards existed ([plan](2022-01-01-seychelles-nhsp-strategic-direction-six-data)); the ministry's own 2022 annual report puts the start in late 2021 with slow progress through 2022 ([report](2023-07-01-moh-annual-performance-report-2022)).

The reform programme launched on 21 July 2026 makes digital health and data-driven decisions one of seven strategic pillars ([reform](2026-07-21-nation-sc-new-era-of-care)), and Cabinet approved repeal of the Health Care Agency in February 2026, folding its functions and records into the ministry ([repeal](2026-02-19-cabinet-health-care-agency-repeal)).

No interoperability specification, standard or exchange with any other system is stated.

summary: The ministry took a [national education management information system live in March 2026](2026-03-18-openemis-seychelles-golive) — the shared platform this question asks about.
developments:
The go-live was announced by the implementation partner rather than by the ministry ([go-live](2026-03-18-openemis-seychelles-golive)).

Around it sits a four-year SMART Plan to modernise teaching, extend technology access in schools nationwide and improve administrative efficiency, paired with a university-built intranet ([plan](2025-03-10-edu-gov-sc-digital-transformation-smart-plan)).

No school-coverage figure, data standard or interface to any other government system is held, so what is established is that a national platform exists and not that it exchanges anything.

summary: [Information-sharing protocols are signed](2025-06-26-worldbank-seychelles-social-protection-isr) with health, employment and education, while the management system behind the social registry remained pending.
developments:
The lender's June 2025 status report records signed inter-agency information-sharing protocols between the social protection agency and health, employment and social affairs, and education, while the agency's management information system needed for the social registry and for broader interoperability remained pending ([status](2025-06-26-worldbank-seychelles-social-protection-isr)).

The platform launched internally in October 2025 through the SeyID portal ([launch](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch)); in March 2026 Cabinet extended vendor support through 2026 and directed the ICT department to lead the transition to government ownership and a long-term national platform ([Cabinet](2026-03-05-asp-connect-cabinet-stabilisation)).

The protocols are signed and the system that would use them is being stabilised.

summary: The [Civil Status Division holds the National Population Database](2026-01-01-ics-civil-status-division) and issues identity cards to all residents under statute.
developments:
The Division's own description confirms custody of the National Population Database and the preparation and issue of identity cards to all residents under the Civil Status Act and the Identity Card Act ([division](2026-01-01-ics-civil-status-division)).

The statistics bureau draws its population releases from those civil-status and immigration administrative records: an all-resident population of 122,730 at 30 June 2025 ([mid-year](2025-08-29-nbs-seychelles-mid-2025-estimated-resident-population)) and 123,097 at 31 December 2025 ([year-end](2026-03-31-nbs-seychelles-end-of-year-population-2025)).

That the register sustains national statistics is evidence it is maintained; no coverage or completeness estimate for it is published.

summary: Immigration and Civil Status issues the identity number and card; a [November 2025 reorganisation](2025-11-06-president-herminie-ministerial-portfolios) put digital transformation under the Vice-President.
developments:
The department remains the issuer of the National Identity Number with the digital credential as a layer above it, and from 17 September 2024 permit holders moved from physical cards to virtual IDs ([notice](2024-09-18-ics-transition-virtual-id-permit-holders)).

The post-election portfolio assignment of November 2025 placed immigration under a Ministry of Homeland Security and Civil Affairs and gave the Vice-President a modernisation portfolio spanning the ICT department and a new Department of Digital Transformation ([portfolios](2025-11-06-president-herminie-ministerial-portfolios)).

The wallet has since added a parent-activated Minor ID against a child's existing identity number ([Minor ID](2026-01-01-seyid-minor-id-wallet)). Two departments now hold parts of one credential chain, and nothing states how they divide it.

summary: The digital identity authenticates with [a password and a second factor](2026-01-01-seyid-security) through an authenticator app, digital certificate or email, on OpenID Connect.
developments:
The platform's own security documentation states password plus two-factor authentication through its authenticator app, a digital certificate or email, built on the OpenID Connect protocol and a commercial PKI ([security](2026-01-01-seyid-security)).

The wallet extends the same credential to a Digital Driving Licence connected live to the licensing authority's system ([wallet](2026-01-01-seyid-idwallet)) and, for minors, to a QR-presented virtual card ([Minor ID](2026-01-01-seyid-minor-id-wallet)).

No assurance level, conformance assessment or independent security review of the platform is published, and the page carries no date of its own.

summary: Digital identity is not issued from birth: a citizen [applies for a physical card with a birth certificate](2026-01-01-ics-national-identity-card), then separately enrols for the digital one.
developments:
The department's own current procedure states that a Seychellois citizen applies for a National Identity Card for the first time using a birth certificate, and then separately signs up for a virtual identity once the identity number and physical card are issued ([procedure](2026-01-01-ics-national-identity-card)).

The wallet's Minor ID lets a parent or guardian activate a child's virtual card, but against an existing national identity number rather than at registration ([Minor ID](2026-01-01-seyid-minor-id-wallet)).

So the chain runs birth certificate, physical card, then digital credential, with a separate enrolment step at the end that nobody is obliged to take.

summary: Digital identity is [issued through the immigration department's own digitalisation programme built with DICT](2024-11-13-national-assembly-verbatim-immigration-civil-status), tied to the identity number and permit validity.
developments:
The department told the National Assembly's budget sitting in November 2024 that digital identity, linked to the National Identity Number and to permit validity, is issued through its own digitalisation programme built jointly with the ICT department ([verbatim](2024-11-13-national-assembly-verbatim-immigration-civil-status)).

Civil registration sits in the same department, whose Division holds the population database ([division](2026-01-01-ics-civil-status-division)), and the 2021 amendment obliges it to digitise every disused register ([amendment](2021-11-04-gazette-civil-status-amendment-act-2021)).

Birth registration and digital identity therefore share a custodian rather than an interface, and nothing held describes a data flow between them.

summary: The credential carries a [Digital Driving Licence connected to the licensing authority's own system](2026-01-01-seyid-idwallet), beyond its originating identity domain.
developments:
The wallet names a Virtual ID Card built with Immigration and Civil Status and a Digital Driving Licence built with, and connected to, the licensing authority's system ([wallet](2026-01-01-seyid-idwallet)); the same authority's business and vehicle licence services require the credential to log in ([licensing](2023-04-19-sla-online-services-seyid-monservis)).

The social protection platform launched in October 2025 is reached through the same portal ([platform](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch)).

A business-facing gateway is being built: the tender board recorded the Ease of Doing Business Portal awarded at USD 1,295,452.86 in December 2025 ([award](2025-12-01-ntb-ease-of-doing-business-portal-award)).

summary: The central bank [licensed a payment service provider in November 2025](2025-11-14-fusepay-psp-licence-approval) for digital accounts and instant payments, under the 2014 payment statute.
developments:
The licence enables digital money accounts, instant and invoice payments and a cheque product, with a first live transaction reported five days after approval ([licence](2025-11-14-fusepay-psp-licence-approval)).

The statutory basis is the National Payment System Act 2014, commenced in August 2014 and since amended by the 2022 electronic money regulations and a 2023 amendment Act ([Act](2014-08-18-seylii-national-payment-system-act-2014)); the December 2025 licensing amendment adds straight-through processing as a condition ([regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025)).

The announcement is the licensee's own, and the central bank publishes no register of licensed payment institutions against which to count them.

summary: The most recent national survey, from 2016, found [94 per cent of adults banked](2016-08-01-finmark-trust-seychelles-financial-literacy-survey-2016) — a decade-old figure with no successor.
developments:
The 2016 baseline survey found 94 per cent of adults banked, the highest rate in the region at the time ([survey](2016-08-01-finmark-trust-seychelles-financial-literacy-survey-2016)); its detailed internet-banking, mobile-money and card figures sit in a section the held capture did not reach.

The central bank's 2025 annual report, submitted on 31 March 2026, is the newest official release covering payment-system activity ([report](2026-03-31-cbs-annual-report-2025)); its transaction-volume tables were not reached by the capture either.

No population-level digital-payment or mobile-money uptake survey since 2016 is held, so a decade-old banking rate is the only national figure available.

summary: The [Financial Consumer Protection Act 2022](2022-04-14-fsa-financial-consumer-protection-act-2022) covers payment providers; the clearest action held is a [2026 warning about an unlicensed exchange](2026-05-26-fsa-mx-global-mexc-enforcement).
developments:
The Act's Schedule Part A expressly covers payment service providers and the operators of payment, clearing and settlement systems under the National Payment System Act ([Act](2022-04-14-fsa-financial-consumer-protection-act-2022)).

In May 2026 the regulator identified the operator of a crypto exchange as unlicensed under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2024 and warned publicly that it could neither investigate nor help recover users' funds ([enforcement](2026-05-26-fsa-mx-global-mexc-enforcement)).

The December 2025 licensing amendment makes safe and reliable IT systems a condition of licence ([regulations](2025-12-15-seychelles-nps-licensing-authorisation-amendment-regs-2025)). Four years after the statute, no complaints statistic, ombudsman route or redress figure under it is published.

summary: Customs duties have been [payable online since June 2024](2024-06-05-src-customs-epayment-launch) and Cabinet now [requires electronic payment of dues of R50,000 and above](2026-04-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-april-2026).
developments:
The revenue commission launched an ePayment facility for customs duties on the ASYCUDA system, delivered under the economic partnership agreement with the European Union ([launch](2024-06-05-src-customs-epayment-launch)).

Electronic filing of tax documents gained its legal basis in regulations made on 24 November 2025 ([regulations](2025-11-24-nationalassembly-si-65-2025-electronic-filing)), and from 1 April 2026 a digital acknowledgment notice replaces the paper assessment letter on lodgement ([notice](2026-03-30-src-streamlines-tax-lodgement-acknowledgement)).

In April 2026 Cabinet approved customs regulations requiring electronic or bank-transfer payment of dues of R50,000 and above ([Cabinet](2026-04-23-seychelles-cabinet-business-22-april-2026)). No share of revenue collected electronically is published.

summary: The [National Population Database](2026-01-01-ics-civil-status-division) sits with the Civil Status Division and sustains the statistics bureau's population releases.
developments:
The Division holds custody of the database and issues identity cards to all residents under the Civil Status Act and the Identity Card Act ([division](2026-01-01-ics-civil-status-division)).

The statistics bureau's 2025 releases draw on those civil-status and immigration administrative records ([releases](2026-03-31-nbs-seychelles-population-2025-releases)), giving 123,097 residents at 31 December 2025 and life expectancy of 77.0 years ([year-end](2026-03-31-nbs-seychelles-end-of-year-population-2025)).

The land-system tender of 2024 named the database as one of the systems a new registry would interface with ([tender](2024-11-27-pou-lmais-tender)), which is the only account held of it being read by anything else.

summary: The [2026 register of voters was certified on 31 March 2026](2026-04-01-nation-sc-ecs-certifies-2026-voters-register), after an online registration portal and tablet voter-tagging debuted in 2025.
developments:
The provisional register went out for inspection from 27 January to 13 February 2026 under section 8(1) of the Elections Act ([gazette](2026-01-12-gazette-no2-provisional-2026-register-of-voters)), and the chief registration officer certified the register on 31 March 2026, with certified copies distributed to eight political parties ([certification](2026-04-01-nation-sc-ecs-certifies-2026-voters-register)).

The Commission's own 2025 report records 73,627 voters certified in March 2025, the register reopened on 14 October 2025 for 1,597 post-election transactions to the end of the year, and an online registration portal and tablet-based voter tagging deployed for the September and October 2025 elections ([report](2026-04-01-ecs-annual-report-2025)).

The 2026 certified total is not stated in what is held.

summary: The land register runs on the [1967 Act](1967-01-01-seychelles-land-registration-act-cap-107); a [land search system](2026-08-01-registrationdivision-new-land-search-system) is announced as coming soon.
developments:
The Land Registration Act of 1967, consolidated to 30 June 2014 and still the operative framework, establishes the Land Registry, the Land Register and the office of Land Registrar and governs registration, dispositions, searches and fees ([Act](1967-01-01-seychelles-land-registration-act-cap-107)).

The lands and ICT departments tendered in November 2024 for a Land Management Administration Information System interfacing with the National Population Database, the digital identity, Immigration and the Registration Division, on a nine-month delivery from award ([tender](2024-11-27-pou-lmais-tender)).

The Registration Division announced a new land search system as coming soon in 2026 ([announcement](2026-08-01-registrationdivision-new-land-search-system)). No award, commissioning or completion statement for either is held.

summary: The [2022 business registration regulations](2022-12-30-si-138-2022-revenue-administration-business-registration) govern the taxpayer register and TIN issuance; lodgement acknowledgment went digital in April 2026.
developments:
The regulations, in force from 1 January 2023, govern registration with the revenue commission, the issuing of tax identification numbers and active, suspended, dormant and deregistered taxpayer status ([regulations](2022-12-30-si-138-2022-revenue-administration-business-registration)).

From 1 April 2026 taxpayers receive a digital acknowledgment notice on lodgement in place of a paper assessment letter ([notice](2026-03-30-src-streamlines-tax-lodgement-acknowledgement)), under regulations of November 2025 giving electronic filing its legal basis ([regulations](2025-11-24-nationalassembly-si-65-2025-electronic-filing)).

No count of registered taxpayers, or of returns filed electronically, is published.

summary: A [statutory duty since 2011](2011-12-27-agency-for-social-protection-act-2011) to hold a beneficiary database has a platform behind it only since October 2025.
developments:
Section 5(e) of the Agency for Social Protection Act 2011 requires the agency to maintain a national database of every applicant for and beneficiary of social assistance ([Act](2011-12-27-agency-for-social-protection-act-2011)).

The Electronic Social Protection System announced in December 2024 for a third-quarter 2025 go-live ([announcement](2024-12-12-asp-esps-sensitisation-launch)) launched internally on 15 October 2025 through the SeyID portal ([launch](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch)); in March 2026 Cabinet extended vendor support through 2026 and directed the ICT department to lead the transition to government ownership ([Cabinet](2026-03-05-asp-connect-cabinet-stabilisation)).

The lender's June 2025 report had the management information system behind the social registry still pending ([status](2025-06-26-worldbank-seychelles-social-protection-isr)).

summary: A [Land Management Administration Information System went to tender in November 2024](2024-11-27-pou-lmais-tender), to interface with the population database and digital identity.
developments:
The tender by the lands and ICT departments sought a system interfacing with the National Population Database, the digital identity, Immigration and the Registration Division, on a nine-month delivery from contract award ([tender](2024-11-27-pou-lmais-tender)).

No award, commissioning or completion statement was found, and the Registration Division's own announcement of a land search system still reads as coming soon ([announcement](2026-08-01-registrationdivision-new-land-search-system)).

Nearly two years after the tender, what is established is an intention with an interface list and no delivery.

summary: The social protection platform [launched internally on 15 October 2025](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch) and Cabinet [extended vendor support through 2026](2026-03-05-asp-connect-cabinet-stabilisation).
developments:
The platform, built with an external firm and announced in December 2024 for a third-quarter 2025 go-live ([announcement](2024-12-12-asp-esps-sensitisation-launch)), launched internally on 15 October 2025 and is reached through the SeyID portal ([launch](2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch)).

In March 2026 Cabinet approved a transitional stabilisation arrangement continuing vendor technical support through 2026 and directing the ICT department to lead the transition to full government ownership and a long-term national platform ([Cabinet](2026-03-05-asp-connect-cabinet-stabilisation)).

A launch that needs a stabilisation arrangement five months later is a system in service and not yet in the state's own hands.

summary: District administrations connect to the [Electronic Government Network](2025-06-17-national-assembly-dict-egn-visit); no separately branded local-government ICT programme is held.
